properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued July 23 at 9:10PM MDT until July 23 at 10:45PM MDT by NWS Boise ID
properties.description:
FFWBOI

The National Weather Service in Boise has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northeastern Ada County in southwestern Idaho...

* Until 1045 PM MDT.

* At 910 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Up to 0.5 inches of rain have
fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 2 to 4 inches in 1 hour.
Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

Excessive rainfall over the area will result in debris flows moving
through the Claremont and Valley burn scars. The debris flows can
consist of rock, mud, vegetation and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban
areas, highways, streets and underpasses as well as
other poor drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Eastern Boise and Aldape Summit.
properties.instruction:

creeks, roads and normally dry washes is likely. The heavy rains
will likely trigger rockslides, mudslides and debris flows in steep
terrain, especially in and around these areas.

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued July 23 at 1:44PM AKDT until July 25 at 12:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Yentna River.

* WHEN...Until noon AKDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water could enter a few low-lying cabins along the Yentna River,
particularly near Lake Creek.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 139 PM AKDT, recent heavy rains have caused rapid river
rises. Minor flooding is expected to continue, especially
along the Yentna River near Lake Creek.
- For Yentna River at Lake Creek:
At 1:30pm the stage was 21.5 feet.
Flood Stage is 20.5 feet.

Impacts:
At 20.5 feet: Anglers Inn & King Point Lodges will have water
in several cabins.

At 22.0 feet: Several lodges and resorts will have water in a
number of cabins with water also encroaching the main lodge
buildings.





- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

- If you live near or along Yentna River, stay alert and be
prepared to take action.

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued July 23 at 10:43AM AKDT until July 23 at 10:45PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is occurring.

* WHERE...Kroto Creek and Moose Creek near Oilwell Road.

* WHEN...Until 1045 PM AKDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Dangerous flows over low-water crossings. Water over roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1033 AM AKDT, river gauge report for Moose Creek at
Oilwell Road indicate rises in water levels from heavy rain
across the advisory area. Minor flooding is occurring,
especially near Kroto Creek and Moose Creek.

- Rainfall will move out of the advisory area by this
afternoon, allowing water levels to begin receding.  However,
drainage from prior heavy rainfall will continue to cause
flooding through this evening.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued July 23 at 8:28AM AKDT until July 24 at 8:30AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is occurring.

* WHERE...Little Susitna River near Northern Matanuska Valley.

* WHEN...Until 830 AM AKDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways, mainly along and near North Sushana Drive.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 826 AM AKDT, river gauge reports indicate rises in water
levels from heavy rain across the advisory area. Minor
flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly, especially
near the Little Susitna River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued July 22 at 9:00PM AKDT until July 24 at 3:15PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Willow Creek, Sheep Creek, Kashwitna River, Montana Creek
and their tributaries from the Parks Highway East between Willow
and the junction of the Talkeetna Spur Road.

* WHEN...Until 315 PM AKDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Dangerous flows over low-water crossings.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 845 PM AKDT, river gauge and social media reports indicate
rises in water levels from heavy rain across the advisory
area. Minor flooding is expected, especially near Willow
Creek, Sheep Creek, Kashwitna River, Montana Creek and their
tributaries.
- For Willow Creek at Parks Highway:
At 8:26pm the stage was 9.0 feet.
Flood Stage is 10.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest around 11.0 feet is expected around 4:00pm
Thursday.

- For Willow Creek near Willow:
At 8:15pm the stage was 4.1 feet.
Flood Stage is 5.9 feet.
Forecast: A crest around 5.9 feet is expected around 10:00am
Thursday.
- Water levels on other rivers, creeks, or streams in the
advisory area, including Montana and Sheep Creeks and
Kashwitna River, may reach or exceed bankfull and remain
elevated through Thursday.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
